take: Phase 3 double-blind RCT across 24 burn centers in North/Central/South America, Europe, and Asia. Adults with deep second-/third-degree burns covering ≥20% TBSA requiring skin grafting were randomized to IV vitamin C 50 mg/kg every 6 hours for 96 hours vs placebo (N=238; mean age 48.9 years, 79% male, mean TBSA 37.0%). Trial stopped early at first prespecified interim analysis for futility/harm. Primary composite outcome (28-day mortality + persistent organ dysfunction at day 28): 40.8% vitamin C vs 29.7% placebo (adjusted RR 1.28, 95% CI 0.99-1.65; p=0.06 — crossed futility/harm threshold). 28-day mortality: 15.0% vs 7.6% (adjusted RR 1.96, 95% CI 1.32-2.90; p=0.001). Hospital mortality: 23.3% vs 16.1% (adjusted RR 1.44, 95% CI 1.03-2.00; p=0.03). Time to hospital discharge not improved.

title: Sodium Bicarbonate for In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: Granfeldt A; Kirkegaard BL; Vallentin MF; (BIHCA Investigators)
pub_types: Equivalence Trial; Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Randomized Controlled Trial
take: Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT across 21 Danish hospitals; 913 randomized, 779 analyzed. Sodium bicarbonate (up to 100 mmol IV) versus placebo during in-hospital cardiac arrest after ≥1 epinephrine dose. Sustained ROSC did not differ (39% vs 37%, RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.88–1.24, p=0.62); 30-day survival (RR 1.25, 95% CI 0.84–1.88) and favorable neurologic outcome (RR 1.39, 95% CI 0.82–2.34) also did not differ, and both CIs cross the null. Alkalosis and hypernatremia were more common with bicarbonate.

title: Management of Chronic Subdural Hematoma With Adjunctive Embolization of Middle Meningeal Artery: The EMMA-Can Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: Shankar JJS; Alcock S; Kashani N; (9-center Canadian trial)
take: Randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint trial at 9 Canadian tertiary centers. Adults with unilateral symptomatic chronic SDH (≥10 mm) undergoing surgical drainage were randomized to adjunctive MMA embolization with Onyx-18 within 72h vs surgery alone (N=186 completers, 93 per arm; mean age 71.8 years, 73% male). Primary outcome: symptomatic SDH recurrence on CT at 90 days. EMMA: 4.3% vs 28% control (risk difference -23.7%, 95% CI -34.1 to -13.9, p<0.001). Radiographic recurrence also markedly lower (14% vs 49.5%). Mortality 4.3% vs 1.1%; SAEs 8.6% vs 5.4% (both NS). Last follow-up July 2025.

title: Adjunctive Intra-Arterial Alteplase After Successful Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke: The CHOICE-2 Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: Renu A; Fernandez-Couto MD; de la Riva P; (14 stroke centers; Spain)
take: Phase 3 open-label RCT at 14 stroke centers in Spain (December 2023 through November 2025). Adults with acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion who achieved eTICI 2b50-3 on thrombectomy within 24h were randomized to adjunctive intra-arterial alteplase 0.225 mg/kg (max 20 mg) vs thrombectomy alone (N=433 treated as randomized; median age 76 years, 51% female). Primary outcome: mRS 0-1 at 90 days. CHOICE-2: 57.5% vs 42.5% excellent functional outcome (adjusted RD 15.0%, 95% CI 5.7-24.3%, p=0.002). However, 90-day mortality was higher in the alteplase group (12.1% vs 6.4%; adjusted RD 5.9%, 95% CI 0.5-11.3%, p=0.03). sICH rates were not significantly different (1.4% vs 0.5%, p=0.33). Residual hypoperfusion reduced with alteplase (28.6% vs 50.5%).

title: Intravenous Tirofiban After Tenecteplase in Acute Ischemic Stroke: The INSTANT Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: Liu X; Zhang F; Zhang C; (Goyal M; Thomalla G; Nguyen TN; Yang Q; Qiu Z; Zeng G; 37 hospitals; China)
take: Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT at 37 Chinese hospitals. N=359 adults with acute ischemic stroke without LVO/MVO/cardioembolic etiology who had inadequate clinical response to IV tenecteplase. Randomized to IV tirofiban (0.3 µg/kg/min bolus then 0.075 µg/kg/min for 47.5h) vs placebo, initiated 4-24h after thrombolysis. Excellent outcome (mRS 0-1 at 90 days): 63.8% vs 52.2% (RR 1.22, 95% CI 1.02-1.46; p=0.03). Symptomatic ICH: 0.9% vs 0%; 90-day mortality: 0.6% vs 1.6%.

title: Plasma Biomarkers of Brain Injury in Critically Ill Children Receiving Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation
authors: Friedman ML; Bell MJ; Brooks BA; (Said A; 11 US children's hospitals)
take: Prospective multicenter observational cohort at 11 US children's hospitals (2019-2023; 18-month follow-up completed 2025). Children aged 2 days to <18 years at ECMO cannulation (N=219 participants, 224 ECMO courses, 1089 serial blood samples). Serial plasma GFAP, NfL, and tau measured throughout ECMO course. In 60 ECMO courses with new ABI on neuroimaging, GFAP rose 6.4%/24h (95% CI 1.4-11.6%) and NfL rose 16.1%/24h (95% CI 10.5-22.0%) preceding imaging-confirmed injury. A 2-fold increase in GFAP (aHR 1.48, CI 1.22-1.79) or NfL (aHR 1.43, CI 1.14-1.79) from first sample was independently associated with unfavorable outcome after adjusting for age and ECMO indication. Tau showed no significant association with outcomes. WashU co-author Ahmed Said. Direct overlap with Neel's PELICAN ECMO study program.

title: Convalescent plasma for people with COVID-19 (Cochrane update)
authors: Iannizzi C; Chai KL; Piechotta V
take: Living-review update incorporating 48 RCTs (24,518 participants; 15 new since prior version). For moderate-to-severe COVID-19, convalescent plasma vs placebo/standard care: no reduction in 28-day all-cause mortality (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.90–1.03; high-certainty), no effect on need for invasive MV or death (RR 1.03, 0.98–1.08; high-certainty), no effect on hospital discharge (RR 1.00, 0.97–1.02; high-certainty). title: Minimizing blood sampling in preterm infants
authors: Nissimov S; Sibrecht G; Weerasekara I
pub_types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review
take: Cochrane systematic review and meta-analysis of 5 RCTs (N=365 preterm infants <29 weeks gestation) evaluating blood-conservation strategies: cord/placental sampling, non-blood fluid sampling, blood-reintroduction micro-sampling devices, and strict sampling protocols. Cord/placental sampling may reduce severe IVH in the first week of life (RR 0.35, 95% CI 0.14–0.89, low certainty) and likely reduces ROP requiring treatment (RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.32–0.85, moderate certainty); effects on mortality and bronchopulmonary dysplasia remain very uncertain, and evidence for reintroduction devices and strict protocols is very low-certainty across all outcomes.

take: State-of-the-art narrative review on ICU nutritional support. impact: confirmatory of the prevailing evidence synthesis

title: Early High-Dose Vitamin C for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: The VITaCCA Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: Rozemeijer S; (multicenter; N=273: 93 placebo; 91 vitamin C 3g; 89 vitamin C 10g IV post-OHCA)
take: Double-blind multicenter phase 2 RCT (N=273 post-OHCA ICU patients). Primary endpoint: change in R-SOFA at 96h. The 10g IV vitamin C arm showed worsened organ function vs placebo (R-SOFA 2.5 points less improvement, 95% CI 0.5–4.5, P=0.01). The 10g group also had worse renal function, higher troponin, and worse neurological outcomes. The 3g arm showed no significant difference. High-dose vitamin C is harmful, not beneficial, in post-OHCA organ dysfunction.
impact: high-dose iv vitamin c (10g) worsened post-arrest organ dysfunction vs placebo in this multicenter phase 2 rct (n=273, r-sofa primary endpoint, ci excludes null for harm; abstract-confirmed); this trial provides evidence against high-dose vitamin c in post-arrest icu care, extending the prior burn-injury victory signal to ohca

take: Retrospective single-center cohort of 54 pediatric ECMO decedents (2009–2024) with cerebral autopsy; 26 had antemortem imaging reviewed by a blinded neuroradiologist using a Neurologic Injury Severity (NIS) framework. Neuropathology revealed frequent ischemic and hemorrhagic injuries most commonly in frontal lobes, deep grey matter, and temporal lobes. NIS scores strongly correlated with global and regional histopathologic severity. Severe pathology corresponded to NIS ≥10. Discordance observed in parieto-occipital, pontine, and cerebellar regions where immunohistochemistry (GFAP, CD68) detected subtle injuries invisible on H&E. VA-ECMO and infant/toddler age associated with more severe injury.

take: Phase 2b double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT (NCT03711903) enrolling 60 patients with acute supratentorial ICH (30 CN-105 vs 30 placebo), treated within 12 hours of onset. take: Multicenter retrospective observational study from 9 Italian tertiary neurocritical care centers (POGASH group), enrolling 326 poor-grade aSAH patients (WFNS IV-V) with intraventricular hemorrhage. Explainable AI-based analysis identified IVH volume >8 mL as a threshold with 92% specificity for predicting in-hospital mortality. IVH volume was also independently associated with long-term disability (mRS) at follow-up. Provides a CT-quantified objective prognostic threshold for mortality risk stratification in highest-severity aSAH patients in the neurological ICU.

title: Patient- and Caregiver-Centered Outcomes in Survivors of Severe Stroke with Respiratory Failure at 6 Months: A Substudy of the SETPOINT2 Trial
authors: (SETPOINT2 substudy)
take: Substudy of the SETPOINT2 early-vs-delayed-tracheostomy RCT (N=366 with 6-month data). 32% had died; among survivors, physical disability and caregiver burden were profound (median EQ-5D-5L 0.3, EQ-VAS 40; 45% of caregivers reported severe/very-severe burden). title: Etiologies, Clinical Characteristics, and Prognostic Impact of Increased Intracranial Pressure in Adults with Encephalitis
authors: (18-hospital multicenter retrospective cohort)
take: Multicenter retrospective study (18 hospitals, Houston/Baltimore, N=647 adults with encephalitis). Opening pressure was measured in only 46%; of those, 18.8% had elevated OP (≥30 cmH2O), which was associated with longer hospital stay, longer mechanical ventilation, and worse Glasgow Outcome Scale scores — yet only 3 patients received targeted ICP-lowering treatment (all 3 survived, 2 with complete/near-complete recovery).

title: Early Prediction of External Ventricular Drain Weaning Trial Outcome in Patients with SAH Based on ICP Pulse Morphological Similarity: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Analysis
authors: Dong K; Sadan O; Horton P
take: Retrospective analysis of 588 SAH patients with 413 successful and 239 failed EVD weaning attempts, quantifying ICP pulse-waveform similarity by Kullback-Leibler divergence from a reference distribution. A support vector machine on pulse features alone reached AUC 0.86 (95% CI 0.79–0.93) and F1 0.77 at 24 hours; clinical features added 5–18% AUC early and little later. Decision-curve analysis showed net benefit from 10 hours onward.
impact: hypothesis-generating, and a good model for waveform-derived prediction

title: Guidelines for Seizure Prophylaxis in Patients with Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: A Statement for Healthcare Professionals from the Neurocritical Care Society
authors: Rowe AS; Zafar SF; Tesoro E
take: GRADE-based systematic review and meta-analysis answering three PICO questions on antiseizure prophylaxis in adult aneurysmal SAH. No difference between ASM and no ASM for early seizure, adverse events, mortality, or functional outcome. Phenytoin/fosphenytoin produced fewer early seizures while levetiracetam carried lower risk of neurologic decline, both at low certainty. All three recommendations are conditional: either ASM or none, either agent if used, and either short or long duration.
impact: practice-relevant as a formal statement of equipoise

authors: Chang DJ; Elkhunovich M; Hotz JC

authors: Vallentin MF; Holmberg MJ; Granfeldt A; (Andersen LW; IVIO trial; Denmark)

title: Between-Hospital Variability in Outcomes After Cardiac Arrest in a Large Clinical Trial Network

title: Integrated CPR coach and compressor training improves CPR quality in a pediatric emergency department
authors: Sahai A; Feldmann K; Klein G
take: Quality-improvement study across 106 pediatric arrests (54 infants, 24 children, 28 adolescents), October 2022 to December 2025, combining CPR coach training, compressor training, and metronome feedback, analyzed with run and statistical control charts. Median depth compliance rose from 14% to 61% and infant mean depth from 3.1 to 4.4 cm; rate compliance rose from 69% to 80% with chest compression fraction held at 89%. Mean depth did not improve in children or adolescents.

title: Tactile stimulation and newborn heart rate responses in the delivery room: an observational video study
authors: Kolstad V; Hoven E; Buskov F
take: Prospective thermal- and visible-light video study of 449 newborns ≥34 weeks at a Norwegian tertiary center, 2022–2024, with dry-electrode ECG heart rates. Stimulation alone was used in 77%, CPAP in 3.1%, and positive-pressure ventilation in 4.4%. Heart rate rose a median 7 bpm among newborns starting below 140 bpm (p < 0.001), and bradycardia in the first minute carried a four-fold likelihood of needing PPV (OR 4.81, 95% CI 1.39–15.3).

title: Prognostic Performance of Plasma and Urinary Biomarkers of Kidney Injury and Function After Out-Of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
authors: Lim SL; Woo KL; Au AY; (Pickering JW; National University Heart Centre Singapore / University of Otago)
take: Prospective observational study of 82 comatose adult OHCA patients. AKI in 65.9%; RRT in 23.2%. Urinary NGAL was the strongest predictor for both CPC 3-5 outcome (AUC 0.79 vs sCr 0.57) and AKI (AUC 0.81). Admission biomarkers collectively predicted AKI better than serum creatinine (AUCs 0.75-0.85 vs 0.65).

title: Temporal Trends in Treatment and Outcomes of Patients with Cardiac Arrest Due to Pulmonary Embolism: A Nationwide Inpatient Database Study
authors: Ishida K; Nishimoto Y; Ohbe H; (Yasunaga H; nationwide Japan inpatient database)

ECMO use increased from 16.0% to 20.8% (p=0.015); thrombolysis decreased from 16.0% to 6.7% (p<0.001). Survival improved from 20.9% to 24.1% (p=0.04); favorable neurological outcomes from 17.4% to 20.6% (p=0.04). Improvements were most pronounced in hospital-acquired PE and ECMO-treated subgroups.

authors: Singh A; Kataria S; John G; Wosser T; Ray S

title: Association of Serum Lactate with Outcome After Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Secondary Analysis of the THAPCA Trial

Serum lactate within 6h of ROSC was strongly associated with unfavorable 12-month neurobehavioral outcome and hospital mortality. Median lactate 7.8 mmol/L (unfavorable) vs 3.1 mmol/L (favorable). OR 1.40 per 1 mmol/L increase (95% CI 1.17–1.69). AUROC robust. Universally available biomarker with neuroprognostication utility in pediatric OHCA.

title: Comparison of Intraosseous Line Placement Location and Rates of Return of Spontaneous Circulation and Survival to Discharge Among Patients with Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
authors: Witherell A; (single-county EMS registry; N=1; 920 OHCA)

Humeral IO associated with higher ROSC (adjusted OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.54–4.22, P=0.0003) and survival to discharge (OR 2.04) vs tibial IO. Single-agency registry; selection by paramedic and patient anatomy introduces unmeasured confounding.

title: Telemedicine-Assisted vs Conventional Telephone Instruction in Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation: The TACTIC Cluster Randomized Trial
authors: Riyapan S; Laopran W; Chantanakomes J; Chakorn T; Somboonkul B; Saelim P

Primary outcome — bystander CPR rate — showed no significant difference (87.3% TA-CPR vs 92.5% DA-CPR, p=0.53). Protocol compliance was lower in the TA-CPR arm (69.1% vs 92.5%), suggesting telemedicine complexity may impair dispatcher efficacy. Pilot in scope; post-arrest neurocritical care endpoints not evaluated.

take: Prospective feasibility cohort at 17 US hospitals (N=338); patients with ARDS or severe AHRF on mechanical ventilation/HFNO. Real-time IL-6 + sTNFR1 + clinical variables used to classify hyperinflammatory vs hypoinflammatory subphenotypes within ~2h of blood draw. Predefined feasibility threshold (>75% successful subphenotyping in final 100 enrolled) was met (82%). Hyperinflammatory subphenotype: 29% of ARDS; worse mortality, fewer organ-support-free days, fewer VFDs. Framework validated across non-COVID viral and non-viral ARDS etiologies.

title: Cefazolin for Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus Bacteremia
authors: SNAP Investigators (multicenter; N=1; 287 enrolled; Bayesian adaptive phase IV equivalence RCT)
pub_types: Randomized Controlled Trial + Multicenter Study (SNAP Bayesian adaptive platform trial)
take: Bayesian adaptive platform equivalence RCT (SNAP). N=1,287 adults with MSSA bacteremia randomized to cefazolin vs antistaphylococcal penicillin (flucloxacillin or cloxacillin). Primary outcome — 90-day mortality — met noninferiority: 15.0% vs 17.0% (adjusted OR 0.81, 95% credible interval 0.59–1.12; P[noninferiority]=99.2%). Pre-specified secondary outcome AKI within 14 days: 13.9% cefazolin vs 19.6% penicillin (adjusted OR 0.67, 95% CrI 0.50–0.89; P[superiority]=99.7%). AKI confirmed as pre-specified secondary endpoint. Adult population only.

authors: Hu W; Jing X; Chen Z; (48-center Chinese trial; Nogueira RG senior)

title: High-Flow Nasal Cannula Versus Noninvasive Ventilation for Prevention of Reintubation in High-Risk Critically Ill Patients (HIGH-FLOW OXY): An Informative Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Nguyen N; Alves de Barros E Lyra N; Downes D
take: Meta-analysis of HFNC versus NIV for postextubation support in adults at high risk of extubation failure. No difference in reintubation (OR 1.19, 95% CI 0.88–1.59), ICU mortality, sepsis, nosocomial pneumonia, or ICU length of stay. Subgroups showed higher reintubation with HFNC among very-high-risk patients (OR 1.63, 95% CI 1.05–2.53) and non-operative obese patients (OR 2.52, 95% CI 1.45–4.38); excluding high-risk-of-bias trials shifted the overall estimate toward harm (OR 1.32, 95% CI 1.02–1.71). Certainty was low throughout.

title: Predictive and Prognostic Performance of the Phoenix Sepsis Criteria and Phoenix Sepsis Score in PICU Patients With Suspected Infection: A Multicenter Prospective Study
authors: Marchetto L; Daverio M; Comoretto R; (Schlapbach LJ; Menon K; Amigoni A; 8 PICUs; Italian TIPNet)
take: Multicenter prospective cohort study at 8 Italian PICU sites (TIPNet; February 2022-April 2024). N=687 children <18 years admitted with suspected infection. PSC showed higher sensitivity and PPV than IPSCC on day 1 (PSC sensitivity 96.4%, PPV 7.6%; IPSCC sensitivity 82.1%, PPV 6.2%). PELOD-2 had the highest AUPRC for mortality (day 1: 0.45; day 2: 0.59). PSS and Phoenix-8 outperformed IPSCC Severe Sepsis. First European cohort validation of PSC and PSS.

title: Effects of a Combined Lifestyle Intervention on Recovery of ICU Survivors: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Christiaanse PMR; van Zutphen T; Bolding HA; (Boerma EC; Beumeler LFE; Frisius Medical Centre; Leeuwarden; Netherlands)
take: Single-centre RCT, N=39 adult long-stay ICU survivors with physical functioning score <67%. 12-week intervention: twice-weekly group exercise + dietary advice + protein supplementation vs standard aftercare. Primary outcome PF score at 12 weeks: significant improvement in intervention group (p=0.024). Daily protein intake increased from 82.3 to 116.7 g/kg in intervention group (p=0.003). Notable ICU characteristic imbalances between arms.

title: Temporal Trends in Outcomes After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Transported to Critical Care Medical Centers in Japan, 2014-2022: A Nationwide Retrospective Observational Study
authors: Shiozumi T; Matsuyama T; Imamura T; (Iwami T; JAAM-OHCA registry; Japan)
take: Nationwide retrospective cohort; N=61,725 adult non-traumatic OHCA transported to Japanese critical care medical centres (2014-2022). Favorable neurological outcomes declined from 3.6% (2014-2016) to 2.5% (2020-2022); aOR 0.83 (95% CI 0.72-0.94) vs 2014-2016. COVID-19 pandemic period credited for decline. ECPR-eligible subgroup improved: aOR 1.43 (95% CI 1.06-1.93) in 2020-2022.

title: Sex Disparities in the Clinical Management and Outcomes of Critically Ill Adults Undergoing Electroencephalography Monitoring
authors: Urbano V; Alvarez V; Schindler K; Rüegg S; Hahn CD; Beuchat I; Benghanem S; Novy J; Rossetti AO
pub_types: Multicenter Study (CERTA trial post hoc analysis)
take: Women with ICH and epileptiform EEG overrepresented but received similar management to men; surviving women had significantly worse 6-month functional outcomes (aOR 0.50 for CPC 1-2, 95% CI 0.28-0.90) despite similar 6-month mortality.

title: Effects of High-Flow Nasal Cannula and Helmet Continuous Positive Airway Pressure in Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure
authors: Coppola S; Pellicchia M; Pozzi T; (Chiumello D; San Paolo University Hospital; Milan)
take: Physiologic crossover RCT in 33 adults with AHRF in a surgical-medical ICU. Each patient received HFNC 60 L/min, Helmet CPAP 5 cmH2O, Helmet CPAP 10 cmH2O, and conventional oxygen therapy in random order. All active supports reduced minute ventilation, inspiratory effort (delta Pes), and improved PaO2/FiO2 vs COT (all p<0.001). Helmet CPAP at 10 cmH2O vs 5 cmH2O did not further reduce inspiratory effort or improve oxygenation but worsened mechanical power.

title: Effect of a Lower Vs. Higher Positive End-Expiratory Pressure Strategy on Clinically Relevant Outcomes in ICU Patients Without Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Bayesian Re-analysis of the RELAx RCT
authors: Caroli A; Algera AG; van Meenen D; (Schultz MJ; Neto AS; Amsterdam UMC / Austin Hospital; Melbourne)
pub_types: Randomized Controlled Trial (post hoc Bayesian re-analysis)
take: Post hoc Bayesian re-analysis of RELAx (N=980 ICU patients without ARDS in 8 ICUs, randomized to lower PEEP 0-5 cmH2O vs higher PEEP 8 cmH2O). For VFD-28, OR for superiority of lower PEEP was 1.08 (95% CrI 0.87-1.35), with probability of benefit 75-78% across priors. For 28-day mortality, probability of benefit of lower PEEP ranged from 72% to 89%. In patients admitted for reasons other than cardiac arrest or intubated for reasons other than respiratory failure, probability of benefit with lower PEEP exceeded 90%.

title: Results of the Pediatric Guideline Adherence and Outcomes (PEGASUS) Program Versus Usual Care Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial in Severe Traumatic Brain Injury
authors: Vavilala MS; Lujan S; Velonjara J; (Bell MJ; Petroni G; 16 South American hospitals)
take: Open-label pragmatic Phase 3 cluster RCT at 16 South American hospitals. N=389 children <18 years with severe TBI (GCS ≤8). No overall difference in first 3-day cumulative ICU TBI guideline adherence (0.1% adjusted difference, 95% CI -3.3 to +3.5%). Isolated severe TBI subgroup: PEGASUS improved adherence by 7.9% (95% CI 1.9-13.8%, p=0.01). Notable imbalance: control patients had less extracranial injury than intervention patients (70.7% vs 82.9%, p=0.005).
impact: null result in pediatric tbi guideline implementation: a facilitated multilevel qi intervention did not improve overall tbi guideline adherence; the isolated tbi subgroup benefit suggests complexity of polytrauma obscures potential effects

title: Temperature Control After In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Outcomes From the Discover In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Cohort
authors: Andrea L; Berg KM; Johnson NJ; (Gong MN; Moskowitz A; 24 hospital systems; 46 hospitals; international)
take: Prospective international observational cohort (October 2023-June 2024). N=1,006 IHCA; 615 (61.1%) comatose and eligible for temperature control; only 44.4% had a documented strategy. Having a strategy associated with reduced fever (aOR 0.63, CI 0.43-0.92) but no difference in survival (32.6% vs 28.1%, aOR 1.19, p=0.42), functional outcome, or neurological outcome. Between-hospital variation in strategy documentation: 0-100%.

title: Disparities in Finding Delirium in Critically Ill Latinos
authors: Fuentes AL; Ellberg CC; Parada H; (Malhotra A; Owens RL; UC San Diego MICU)
take: Prospective observational cohort at 2 MICUs (UC San Diego, August 2024-January 2025). N=142 ICU patients (71 English-speakers, 71 Spanish-speakers) + 100 caregivers. Delirium prevalence 39%. Agreement between usual-care CAM-ICU and reference-standard: kappa 0.71 (English) vs 0.11 (Spanish), with 72% of delirium missed in Spanish-speakers. FAM-CAM (caregiver-administered) in Spanish-speakers: kappa 0.68 vs 0.11 for usual care (p<0.05), reducing missed delirium by 47%. Spanish-speakers more deeply sedated and had higher odds of restraint use (OR 4.53, 95% CI 1.91-10.74).

title: External Validation, Molecular Signatures, and Therapeutic Relevance of Pediatric Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury Subphenotypes
authors: Stanski NL; Zhang B; Ouyang J; Standage SW; Cvijanovich NZ; Fitzgerald JC; Bigham MT; Jain PN; Lutfi R; Allen GL; Thomas NJ; Baines T; Haileselassie B; Weiss SL; Lautz AJ; Kaplan JM; Zingarelli B; Atreya MR; Sanchez-Pinto LN; Goldstein SL; Liu KD
take: External validation of pediatric sepsis-associated AKI (pSAKI) molecular subphenotypes across 10 US PICUs (N=871), incorporating biomarker signatures and heterogeneity-of-treatment-effect analyses for corticosteroids and vasopressin.

title: Technology-Enhanced Strategies to Optimize Positive End-Expiratory Pressure in Patients Receiving Invasive Mechanical Ventilation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Boulton AJ; Elfeky A; Court R; (Goligher EC; Scholefield BR; University of Warwick / University of Toronto)
take: Systematic review of 34 RCTs (N=2,951 patients) evaluating 7 technology-enhanced PEEP optimization strategies (esophageal balloon, EIT, P-V curve, closed-loop ventilation, others) vs standard care in ICU patients on invasive MV. Duration of MV: no effect (mean difference -0.06 days, 95% CI -0.20 to 0.09; very low certainty; 3 studies only). 28-day mortality (10 studies; 1,719 patients): technology-enhanced PEEP reduced mortality (RR 0.69; 95% CI 0.52–0.93; very low certainty). No evidence in children or for cost-effectiveness. PROSPERO CRD42024555390.

title: Prognostic Factors Associated With Mortality Among Patients With Necrotizing Soft-Tissue Infection: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Kruger N; Durr K; Fernando SM; (Rochwerg B; Tran A)
take: 41 observational cohort studies, N=168,261 patients with NSTI. Patient factors with moderate-to-high certainty of association with increased mortality: older age, chronic liver disease, CKD, high Charlson Comorbidity Index, immunosuppression. Disease factors: hypotension, bacteremia, AKI, coagulopathy, thrombocytopenia, and shock. Graded certainty using GRADE methodology.

title: Prone Positioning in a North American Cohort of Hypoxemic Patients on Mechanical Ventilation
authors: Barker AK; Nishimura A; Nuppnau M; Buell KG; Lyons PG; Liao WT; Park-Egan B; Schmid BE; Ingraham NE; Chaudhari V; Gao CA; Ortiz AC; Weissman GE; Chhikara K; Rojas JC; Amaral ACKB; Parker WF; Iwashyna TJ; Hager DN; Sjoding MW; Hochberg CH; on behalf of the Common Longitudinal ICU data Format (CLIF) Consortium
take: Retrospective cohort from the 37-hospital CLIF Consortium (N=5944) examining prone-positioning utilization rates in hypoxemic mechanically ventilated patients before and after the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Difficulty Paying for Medical Care: Associations With Psychological Distress and Perceptions of Healthcare Among ICU Caregivers
authors: Hardt MM; Lichtenthal WG; Saviano S; (Prigerson HG; 3 US medical ICUs)
take: Cross-sectional baseline analysis from a multicenter RCT (N=97 ICU family caregivers). 63.9% reported difficulty paying for patient medical care. Financial strain correlated with PTSD symptom severity (r=0.35, p<0.001), anxiety (r=0.22, p<0.05), depressive symptoms (r=0.27, p<0.01), decisional regret (r=0.30, p<0.05), and medical mistrust (r=0.30, p<0.01).

title: Effects of the ABCDEF Bundle on Delirium, Function, and Quality of Life in Australian ICU Patients: A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Sosnowski KJ; Ranse KL; Mitchell ML; Ware RS; White HT; Morrison LA; Schweitzer VC; Chaboyer WP
pub_types: Pragmatic Clinical Trial; Randomized Controlled Trial
take: Single-center pragmatic RCT in an 8-bed Australian ICU evaluating the ABCDEF bundle vs usual care, with delirium incidence/duration as the primary outcome and functional status and quality of life as secondary outcomes.

title: Point-of-Care EEG Artificial Intelligence Measure of Seizure Burden Associates With Clinical Outcome at Discharge
authors: Parvizi J; Armenta Salas M; Aparicio MK; Zafar SF; Desai M; Karunakaran S; Gupta A; Kamousi B; Hirsch LJ; Struck AF
take: Secondary analysis of the multicenter SAFER-EEG study (N=359 with complete data of 400 enrolled) evaluating an AI-derived point-of-care EEG seizure-burden measure against discharge modified Rankin Scale in critically ill patients.

title: Nebulized Heparin in Adults With Acute Respiratory Failure: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials
authors: Fresilli S; Belletti A; Labanca R; Monti G; Schultz MJ; Corbo F; Luciano AP; Ferrara B; Turi S; Landoni G; for the Nebulized Heparin Study Group
take: Meta-analysis of 16 RCTs (787 vs 833 patients) evaluating nebulized heparin vs placebo/usual care in adults with acute respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation.
impact: confirmatory signal, hypothesis-generating for practice change

title: Association Between Sex and Clinical Outcomes for Critically Ill Patients in India: A Registry-Embedded Cohort Study (IRIS)
authors: Tirupakuzhi Vijayaraghavan BK; Patodia S; Gamage Dona D; (Adhikari NKJ; Fowler R; 45 ICUs; N=82; 151)
take: Retrospective registry cohort of 82,151 ICU patients from 45 ICUs in India (IRIS registry). 38.2% female. Adjusted ICU mortality similar (9.5% vs 10.3%; adjOR 0.95, 95% CI 0.90–1.00; p=0.07). Females less commonly received invasive ventilation (adjOR 0.78), renal replacement therapy (adjOR 0.73), and vasopressors (adjOR 0.95). Non-invasive ventilation received more by females (OR 1.23). Similar adjusted outcomes despite lower organ support rates.

title: Comparison of Intensive Versus Conventional Glycemic Control Targets: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the 2024 Society of Critical Care Medicine Guidelines on Glycemic Control for Critically Ill Adults
authors: Sirimaturos M; Honarmand K; Long MT
pub_types: Journal Article / Systematic Review / Meta-Analysis / Comparative Study
take: Forty-five RCTs, 32,215 critically ill adults on insulin infusions. Intensive versus conventional targets showed no difference in hospital or ICU mortality. Intensive control was associated with shorter ICU stay, fewer infections, and less critical illness polyneuropathy, but a 3.6-fold higher risk of severe hypoglycemia, and most studies driving the significant differences carried serious inconsistency or risk of bias.

title: Prevalence, Risk Factors, and Mortality of Veno-Venous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Escalation in Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Multicenter Cohort Study From the Chinese Society of Extracorporeal Life Support Registry
authors: Ma S; Pan Y; He J
take: Registry cohort of 3,333 adults on VV-ECMO for ARDS across 112 Chinese centers, 2017–2023. Escalation to VA (n = 41), VAV (n = 68), or VVA (n = 48) occurred in 157 patients (4.7%). Overall in-hospital mortality was 47.9%; both escalation and lower center volume were independently associated with mortality, and centers doing >15 cases/year had lower odds of escalation than those doing <6 (OR 0.596, 95% CI 0.382–0.930).

title: Sodium Bicarbonate for Acute Metabolic Acidosis in Critically Ill Adults: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials
authors: Chen JJ; Lee TH; Chang CH
take: Four RCTs, 1,111 patients, with trial sequential and Bayesian sensitivity analyses. Sodium bicarbonate reduced RRT use (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.61–0.78) with TSA supporting firm evidence. Mortality showed a nonsignificant trend (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.55–1.30) with the cumulative sample far below the required information size; Bayesian posterior probabilities of benefit were 90.4% for mortality and 94.6% for RRT.
impact: practice-relevant for the rrt endpoint only

title: Efficacy and Safety of Systemic Prophylactic Antibacterials in Mechanically Ventilated Patients: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Yu Q; Wu Z; Ge Q
take: Systemic prophylactic antibacterials reduced overall VAP (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.55–0.77) and early VAP (RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.41–0.66), both moderate certainty, without reducing in-hospital mortality (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.68–1.06) or ventilation duration. Subgroup analysis suggested benefit concentrated in brain-injured patients. No increase in resistance or adverse events was observed, though the authors note safety reporting was incomplete.

title: Impact of Time to Antibiotics on In-hospital Mortality in Neutropenic Sepsis: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study
authors: Kim D; Kim YJ; Ryoo SM
pub_types: Journal Article / Multicenter Study / Observational Study
take: Prospective cohort of 942 patients with neutropenic sepsis across 20 Korean hospitals, grouped by time to antibiotics (<1 h, 1–3 h, ≥3 h). Under IPTW, in-hospital mortality odds rose with delay: OR 1.26 (95% CI 1.04–1.53) for intermediate and 1.50 (95% CI 1.22–1.85) for delayed versus early. The association was stronger in septic shock and hematologic malignancy; a causal forest flagged elevated lactate as a candidate effect modifier, though the interaction test was not significant.

title: Determinants of Delayed Recovery of Consciousness After Analgosedation Discontinuation in the ICU: Insights From Patients With COVID-19 Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure
authors: [First author not listed in section metadata]; (3 academic centers; N=784 COVID-19 MV ICU patients)
take: Retrospective cohort (3 academic centers; N=784 COVID-19 ICU patients on MV). Delayed recovery of consciousness (later than pharmacokinetically predicted) in 34%. Late RoC independently associated with older age, hypoxemia severity, and AKI. Dexmedetomidine adjunct associated with earlier consciousness recovery. COVID-19 served as study vehicle; primary topic is sedation pharmacokinetics in MV patients.

title: Clinical Prediction Models for Prognostication After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Niznick N; Sadeghirad B; Rochwerg B
take: Thirty-nine observational cohorts, 95,037 patients, 11 prediction models, restricted to models with at least two external validations. An OHCA score ≥32 gave pooled sensitivity 64.9% and specificity 89.5%; CAHP ≥150 gave sensitivity 81.3% and specificity 77.0% (moderate certainty). Pooled AUROCs ranged 0.75–0.88 with substantial heterogeneity.

title: Association Between Emergency Department-to-ICU Transfer Time and Hospital Mortality Across ICU Admission Diagnoses: A Post Hoc Subgroup Analysis
authors: van Herwerden MC; (12 Dutch hospitals; N=18; 798)
take: Retrospective multicenter cohort (12 Dutch hospitals; N=18,798). In OHCA patients (n=3,818), prolonged ED-to-ICU transfer time associated with higher mortality in academic hospitals (OR 2.94 for >3.4h; P<0.001) but inversely in non-academic teaching hospitals. No association detected for ICH, sepsis, or respiratory failure. Hospital type modifies the transfer-time–mortality relationship with opposing directions.

title: Diagnostic and Prognostic Value of the Venous Excess Ultrasound Grading System: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Klompmaker P; Opschoor K; Dalen JT; (Tuinman PR; Amsterdam UMC)
take: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 32 studies (N=3,142 patients) evaluating VExUS for venous congestion. In cardiac patients: VExUS ≥2 associated with AKI (OR 4.44, 95% CI 2.34-8.43; moderate certainty) and mortality (OR 3.17, CI 1.30-7.75; low certainty). In critically ill patients: VExUS ≥2 NOT significantly associated with AKI (OR 1.45, CI 0.70-2.99; very low certainty) or mortality (OR 1.25, CI 0.77-2.03; low certainty). Diagnostic accuracy for elevated CVP/RA pressure: sensitivity 78-95%, specificity 80-90%.

title: Concordance Between Bedside and Electronic Detection of Intracranial Pressure Crises: Insights From the BOOST-II Trial
authors: [First author not listed in section metadata]; (10 US ICUs; N=70 severe TBI patients)
take: Post-hoc analysis (BOOST-II; 10 US ICUs; N=70 severe TBI). Bedside clinicians confirmed only 47% of ICP crises identified electronically. In 31% of discordant episodes, electronic monitoring showed ICP consistently below threshold, suggesting false-positive detection or delayed bedside response. Fundamental reliability concern for current bedside-only ICP crisis identification.

title: Continuing Vs. Withholding Home Beta-Blockers at Admission for Suspected Infection: A Target Trial Emulation
authors: Christian-Miller N; Lee KT; Pashun R; (Admon AJ; University of Michigan)
take: Target trial emulation at a single academic tertiary care ED (N=4,635 patients on chronic beta-blockers with suspected infection). Beta-blocker continuation (25.3%) vs discontinuation within 48h. Continuation associated with reduced 90-day all-cause mortality (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.61-0.98, p=0.03) and shorter hospital stay (IRR 0.39, p<0.001). In-hospital mortality not significantly different (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.30-1.20, p=0.15).

title: Health-Economic Value of Transvenous Diaphragm Neurostimulation in Ventilator Weaning
authors: Pietzsch JB; Ryschon AM; Mehta N
take: Cost-consequence analysis built on RESCUE-3 RCT data and real-world claims, modeling transvenous diaphragm neurostimulation (tDNS) versus standard-of-care weaning. authors: Nakamura S; Inoue K; Takahashi K

title: Large Single-Center Experience With Extubation During Neonatal and Pediatric Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation
authors: Holton C; Orrick J; Newton D; Miller JO (Children's Mercy Hospital; Kansas City)
take: Largest reported single-center pediatric extubation-on-ECMO cohort (N=40 over 10 years, 8.6% of all ECMO runs). Extubated patients tended to be older and cannulated for pulmonary support. Survival to discharge 75% vs non-extubated cohort (p=0.044). After adjustment for ECMO run duration, extubated patients had more GI hemorrhage and CRRT use; no excess mechanical, neurologic, cardiovascular, or pulmonary complications.

title: Pediatric Critical Hematology Oncology Referral Pathway for Extracorporeal Life Support: Standardized Evaluation and Transfer Can Improve Survival
authors: Sandhu HS; Fan K; Shah S; (Morrison RR; Ghafoor S; Le Bonheur Children's Hospital / St. Jude Children's Research Hospital; Memphis)
take: Retrospective chart review of 46 pediatric heme-onc patients transferred for ECLS evaluation (2010–2021). Pre-CHORPE pathway (n=17): 6 placed on ECLS, 0 survived to discharge. Post-CHORPE (n=28): 9 on ECLS, 5 survived to discharge (OR 15.9, p=0.03). Fewer transfer complications post-implementation (p=0.023). Standardized referral criteria also reduced inappropriate ECLS use.

title: Outcomes of a Second Run of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Neonates: A Propensity Score Matched Analysis of a Nationwide Registry
authors: Thobani H; Khan MO; Tirrell TF
take: ELSO Registry analysis of 12,292 neonates undergoing 12,668 ECMO runs, 2009–2019, comparing single-run with two-run patients. Survival to discharge was 33.8% after a second run versus 62.9% for single-run patients; propensity-matched odds of death were 3.53 (95% CI 2.75–4.56) irrespective of physiologic status or indication. Neonates needing a second run had shorter first runs and were more often venoarterial.

title: Hemodynamic Ramp Test in Cardiogenic Shock Supported by Microaxial Flow Pump: Protocol Description, Feasibility, and Hemodynamic Response
authors: Ikeda Y; Iikura S; Nakahara S
take: Single-center prospective study of a standardized Impella ramp protocol in 54 cardiogenic shock patients meeting pretest stability criteria, stepping P-level from P8 to P2 at 5-minute intervals under pulmonary artery catheter monitoring. Forty-six (85%) completed the protocol; eight stopped for predefined safety criteria and recovered on return to baseline. Across the cohort, pulse pressure rose 12.2 mm Hg, cardiac power output fell 0.09 W, and wedge pressure rose 2.5 mm Hg.

title: Subphenotype-Specific Risk of Intracranial Hemorrhage During Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
authors: Nishikimi M; Ohshimo S; Fukumoto W
pub_types: Journal Article / Multicenter Study / Observational Study
take: Japanese multicenter cohort of 536 adults on VV-ECMO for severe ARDS, classified into fibrotic, dry, and wet subphenotypes, analyzed with Fine-Gray competing-risk models under IPTW. ICH occurred in 3.7% overall and carried 65.0% mortality versus 27.5% without. Incidence was 8.7% in the fibrotic group versus 0.5% dry and 1.8% wet; fibrotic phenotype carried a hazard ratio of 4.33 (95% CI 1.47–12.69).

title: Is Veno-Venous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Always the Right Choice for Pediatric Patients With Refractory Respiratory Failure? An Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry Analysis
authors: Assy J; Yit G; Alunni Fegatelli D; (Alessandri F; multi-institution)
take: ELSO Registry retrospective analysis (2014–2024), 5,162 pediatric VV-ECMO patients. Conversion to VA or alternative configuration occurred in 8.1% (n=421) and was associated with significantly higher in-hospital mortality (51.1% vs 26.7%, p<0.001), longer ECMO runs (13 vs 8 days), and longer hospital stay. Pre-ECMO lactate was an independent predictor of conversion (OR 1.056 per unit, CI 0.999–1.112). Patients with both low MAP and high lactate before ECMO deployment may not be appropriate VV candidates.

title: Preoperative Use of Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Postinfarct Ventricular Septal Rupture: Insights From the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry
authors: Gemelli M; Ronco D; Matteucci M; (Lorusso R; ELSO Registry multicenter; 2000-2025)
take: ELSO Registry retrospective analysis (2000-2025). N=370 adults with post-AMI VSR receiving preoperative VA-ECMO; 66% in cardiogenic shock at ECMO initiation. In-hospital mortality 68%. Survivors were younger (62 vs 67 years), had lower pre-ECMO arrest rates (7% vs 21%), lower tamponade rates (2% vs 8%), and lower RRT rates (21% vs 37%).

title: Early Experience of a Fully Magnetically Levitated Temporary Ventricular Assist Device in China: A Multicenter Single-Arm Study
authors: Li P; Wu T; Wang IW
take: Prospective multicenter single-arm study (N=40, 7 Chinese centers) of the MoyoAssist temporary VAD in postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock (50%) and bridge-to-transplant (32.5%). 30-day success rate 62.5%, no severe device-related adverse events; success exceeded target in both indication subgroups.

title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Immunocompromised Patients With Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
authors: Fei S; Huang C; Zhang X
take: Seventeen cohort studies, 5,136 adults (1,311 immunocompromised) meeting Berlin criteria. Immunocompromised patients had lower ECMO weaning (RR 0.77), higher hospital mortality (RR 1.38), and higher 6-month mortality (RR 1.31). Risk was graded by immunocompromise type: hematologic malignancy OR 3.76, autoimmune disease OR 2.50, solid organ transplant OR 1.40.

title: Impact of Delayed Heparin Bridging on Bleeding and Stroke After Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation
authors: Jahangiri P; Luo Y; Sjatskig J; (Caliskan K; Erasmus MC)
take: 193 consecutive HeartMate 3 recipients compared by anticoagulation protocol (old: heparin at 24–48h if chest drain acceptable; new: withhold heparin ≥48h). Early reoperation for bleeding: 42.4% vs 24.1% (p=0.006). Stroke: 6.6% vs 8.0% (p=0.72). ICU stay: 7 vs 5 days (p=0.03). Hospital stay: 28 vs 24 days (p=0.04).

title: Pediatric Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (ECPR): Understanding Variations in Systems and Clinical Practice
authors: O’Callaghan M; Belohlavek J; Cvetkovic M; Davidson M; Guerguerian AM; Hoskote A; Pollak U; Raman L; Roeleveld PP; Thiruchelvam T; Desai A
take: A survey of 53 ELSO-affiliated centers found wide variation in pediatric ECPR practice, including circuit readiness, institutional protocols, and use of cooling.

title: Risk Score to Assess Extracorporeal Life Support Need After Norwood Operation on Arrival to Pediatric Cardiac Intensive Care Unit
authors: Beshish AG; Horan V; Faisthalab M; (Garcia RU; Aljiffry A; Children's Healthcare of Atlanta/Emory)
take: Retrospective cohort of 322 neonates post-Norwood (2010–2023); 71 (22%) required postoperative ECLS within 7 days. Multivariable logistic regression identified 6 predictors (AV valve regurgitation, mBTT shunt, CPB time >173.5 min, vasoactive inotropic score >19.5 on CICU arrival, delayed sternal closure, iNO use). Bedside risk score (range 0–29): low-risk (0–10) 8% ECLS rate, moderate (12–19) 31%, high (20–29) 65%. AUC 0.78.

title: Clinical Outcomes and Risk Factors in Pediatric Postcardiotomy Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Nationwide Retrospective Cohort Study
authors: Xu B; Zhou X; Yu X; (Hou X; Li C; Beijing Anzhen Hospital; Capital Medical University)
take: Nationwide retrospective cohort from the Chinese Society of Extracorporeal Life Support registry (December 2016-April 2024). N=487 pediatric patients (<18 years) receiving postcardiotomy ECMO (PC-ECMO). Overall in-hospital survival 48.9%; neonatal mortality 61.4%. Independent predictors of in-hospital mortality: RACHS-2 category 4-5 (OR 2.976, p<0.001), aortic cross-clamp time >90 min (OR 1.931, p=0.007), elevated lactate at 24h post-ECMO (OR 1.221 per mmol/L, p<0.001), and renal complications (OR 3.135, p<0.001). Combined predictive model AUC 0.737.

title: Anticoagulation Changes and Biochemical Signals Preceding Hospital-Acquired Infections in Pediatric Extracorporeal Support
authors: Davidson SM; Miller JO; Bauer PN; (Rilinger JF; Children's Mercy Hospital; Kansas City)
take: Single-center retrospective propensity-matched case-control study (N=62 HAI cases vs 169 matched controls). Patients with HAIs had significantly more ECMO circuit changes (20 vs 3, p<0.001) and greater anticoagulation variability: more heparin adjustments on ECMO (p<0.001) and bivalirudin adjustments on CRRT (p=0.014). Absolute neutrophil count elevated in infected patients (7.0 vs 4.8 K/µL, p=0.003); CRP, PCT, and WBC did not differ. Anticoagulation variability and circuit instability preceded HAI diagnosis.

authors: Huang V; Huang JX; Roem J; Ng DK; Bembea MM

title: Incidence and Mortality Outcomes of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Infants With Congenital Lung Malformations: A Registry Study
authors: Giron A; Chen Z; Yu PT; Guner YS
pub_types: Journal Article (ELSO registry cohort; effectively multicenter)
take: ELSO registry cohort (2000–2024) of 451 infants placed on ECMO for congenital lung malformations, 88% neonates. Overall survival to discharge was 47%, varying by malformation subtype. Postnatal corticosteroid exposure and lower weight at ECMO initiation were associated with survival; ECPR, hemorrhagic complications, and neurologic complications were associated with mortality.

title: Outcomes of Temporary Right Ventricular Assist Device at the Time of Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation
authors: Usman AA; Cevasco M; Bermudez C
take: Retrospective single-center cohort (N=102 receiving temporary RVAD at durable LVAD implant, 2017-2025). Preoperative mechanical circulatory support (VA-ECMO or micro-axial pump) was independently associated with improved 1-year survival (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.17-0.83). Authors explicitly note causality cannot be established from this retrospective design.

title: The Role of Recirculation-Guided Blood Flow Adjustment in Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Pilot Study
authors: Behnel N; Heilmann W; Skrypnikov V
take: Prospective single-center pilot (N=21 severe ARDS patients on high-flow V-V ECMO) using ultrasound-dilution-measured recirculation to guide stepwise flow reduction. Recirculation was measurable in 90% (median 14%), was significantly higher with RV dysfunction (25% vs 9%, p=0.024), and flow reduction was completed in 75% of attempts (9/12) while maintaining oxygenation (SaO2 99%→98%).

title: Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Timing in Infarct-Related Cardiogenic Shock: Before Versus After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
authors: Pan C; Zhao J; Bai N

title: Rehabilitation Intensity and Discharge Outcomes in Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Used as a Bridge to Recovery

title: Beating the Odds: Survival After Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Decannulation Due to Poor Prognosis in Children—An Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry Study

authors: Rose AT; Lakhani A; Conroy S

take: Single-center retrospective cohort of 154 ECMO runs (151 pediatric patients) at a quaternary children's hospital PICU/NICU/cardiac ICU (November 2017-December 2022). New nosocomial infections detected in 41% of runs. Diagnostic accuracy of standard inflammatory markers was poor: CRP AUC 0.66 (95% CI 0.60-0.72), procalcitonin AUC 0.62 (0.53-0.72), WBC AUC 0.51 (0.44-0.57). However, normal values demonstrated useful negative predictive value: PCT <1.77 ng/mL had 95% NPV, CRP <36.5 mg/L had 97% NPV, WBC <11.02 K/µL had 95% NPV. Antibiotics were administered on 84.7% of ECMO days; 98.7% of patients received more than 48 hours of antibiotics.

title: Electrical Impedance Tomography Accurately Reflects Regional Ventilation Distribution Compared With Computed Tomography in Non-Intubated Subjects
authors: Morais CCA; Rattes C; Rocha T
take: Paired EIT and CT (end-expiratory and end-inspiratory pauses) in 32 spontaneously breathing non-intubated subjects. At a 15-cm CT lung length the posterior ROI bias was 0.80% (limits of agreement −9.26% to 10.87%) and the right ROI bias −1.33% (−9.15% to 6.47%). Sex, BMI, fat percentage, and thoracic or abdominal circumference did not affect the EIT–CT difference; intra- and inter-examiner bias stayed under 1.5%.

title: Femoral Muscle Volume Change and Postextubation Respiratory Support in Infants After Cardiac Surgery
authors: Yamamoto N; Tani M; Mihara T
take: Prospective single-center study of 42 infants ventilated >48 hours after congenital heart surgery, 26 (61.9%) requiring postextubation support. Femoral muscle index and its change performed no better than chance (AUC 0.50, 95% CI 0.31–0.69; and 0.63, 95% CI 0.45–0.80), while weight-adjusted tidal volume and breathing frequency before extubation predicted well (AUC 0.81 and 0.72).

title: Effects of Heat-Moisture Exchangers and Dead Space Compensation on CO2 Clearance and Mechanical Power in Critically Ill Intubated Subjects
authors: Dorado JH; Perez J; Steinberg D; Plotnikow GA; Bertozzi M; Accoce M
take: Adding a heat-moisture exchanger impaired CO2 elimination in intubated adults on controlled ventilation, and compensating with either higher tidal volume or higher breathing frequency raised mechanical power, with tidal-volume compensation more effective for CO2 clearance but increasing elastic mechanical power.

title: Reverse Triggering With and Without Breath Stacking During Pressure-Controlled Ventilation: Exposure Burden and Associations With Ventilation Outcomes
authors: Zhang S; Yuan S; Baedorf Kassis E; (Talmor D; Su L; Long Y; PUMCH + Harvard/Beth Israel Deaconess)
take: Prospective observational; 429 ICU adults on PCV with >24h waveform monitoring. Reverse triggering in 40.6%; breath stacking (RT-BS) in 80 subjects. RT-BS associated with higher driving pressure (8.5 vs 7.0 cmH2O), higher PIP, longer MV duration (7 vs 4 days, p=0.015). Fentanyl and lower P/F ratio were independent risk factors. Breath-stacked VT threshold of 141 mL associated with prolonged MV on ROC analysis.

title: The Accuracy of Plateau and Driving Pressures During Assisted and Spontaneous Ventilation Depends on the Degree of Inspiratory Effort and Duration of the Inspiratory Hold
authors: [First author not listed in section metadata]; (ASL-5000 simulator + pediatric ARDS trial waveforms)
pub_types: Bench Study + Pediatric ARDS Secondary Analysis
take: Combined bench study (ASL-5000 lung simulator) and secondary analysis of pediatric ARDS trial waveforms. During passive breathing, Pplat equilibrates within 0–400 ms. During assisted/spontaneous breathing with high inspiratory effort, Pplat equilibration requires >1,500 ms; compliance is overestimated and driving pressure is systematically inaccurate. Standard Pplat-derived driving pressure is unreliable during assisted/spontaneous ventilation.

title: Association of Extubation Timing and Treatment Failure After Successful Extubation Readiness Trial in Pediatric Patients
authors: [First author not listed in section metadata]; (single quaternary PICU; N=261)
take: Retrospective cohort of 261 children at a single quaternary PICU. Early extubation (<6h post-ERT) was not associated with increased treatment failure (IPTW-adjusted OR 1.30, 95% CI 0.66–2.57) vs late extubation. Early extubation was associated with significantly reduced ICU stay (55.5 vs 98.5h, P<0.01).

title: Effect of High-Flow Nasal Cannula on Expiratory Muscle Activity in Critically Ill Subjects
authors: [First author not listed in section metadata]; (single ICU; N=30)
take: RCT crossover (N=30 ICU patients on HFNC; three flow rates 30, 40, 50 L/min in random order). HFNC did not uniformly reduce expiratory muscle activity. At 50 L/min, DTF decreased (13% vs 25%, P=0.042). Patients with baseline TF>10% showed abdominal muscle unloading at 40–50 L/min. Diaphragm ultrasound may identify flow-responders.

title: Automated Detection of Trigger Asynchronies During Initiation of Noninvasive Nocturnal Ventilation
authors: Soleimani F; Warnaar R; Hazenberg A
take: Fourteen subjects with COPD starting nocturnal NIV, with asynchrony estimated three ways. Median patient-ventilator asynchrony was 12.7% from pressure-flow alone, 13.7% adding thoracic respiratory inductance plethysmography, and 22.7% adding intercostal or diaphragm surface EMG. The analyzable breath sets differed across modalities, which the authors flag as limiting direct comparison.

take: 53 non-randomized studies used oxygenation (PaO2/FiO2 change supine-to-prone) as the response definition; pooled responder proportion 68% (95% CI 63–72%). Alternative physiological definitions (CO2 clearance, respiratory mechanics, V/Q matching) yielded responder proportions of 45–53%. Of 26 studies providing unadjusted mortality data, 11 (42%) reported lower mortality in responders. Sensitivity analysis restricted to 5 high-bias-risk studies: OR 0.41 (95% CI 0.25–0.68; I²=78%). Overall: high heterogeneity, high risk of bias, no robust survival signal from physiological response alone.

title: One year quality of life outcomes in critically ill children: a multicenter prospective cohort study (OCEANIC)
authors: Manning JC; Latour JM; Draper E; (Curley MAQ; 10 English PICUs; N=326)
take: Prospective cohort, 10 English PICUs (2019–2022, follow-up to 2023); 326 children enrolled, 220 with ≥3 HRQoL assessments. PedsQL fell from 73.3 at baseline to 54.3 at PICU discharge, recovering to 70.4 at 6 months and 69.8 at 12 months. At 12 months, 58.1% of respondents remained below their pre-PICU baseline. Physical and school functioning showed the most persistent impairment; cognitive functioning recovered by 1 month; fatigue largely resolved by 6 months. SHAP analysis identified higher baseline HRQoL, older age, and prolonged PICU exposure as features associated with persistent below-baseline HRQoL.

title: Predictive validity of daily sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA)-2 score for 30-day mortality
authors: Helleberg J; Sundelin A; Soltani N; Rooyackers O; Martensson J (Karolinska University Hospital / Karolinska Institutet)

From day 2 onward, both scores performed similarly. Reclassification between SOFA-1 and SOFA-2 occurred in 75-79% of admissions. Day-1 AUROC varied by subgroup: trauma 0.81, sepsis 0.72.

title: Hyperlactatemia in sepsis and shock: a renal metabolic perspective
authors: Payen D; Rimmele T; Gomez H (University of Pittsburgh / CHU Nice)
take: Narrative review synthesizing the underappreciated renal contribution to lactate clearance in critically ill patients. Proximal tubular cells are major lactate consumers; sepsis-induced AKI impairs systemic lactate homeostasis by eliminating this clearance pathway. Reviews urinary lactate as a marker of proximal tubular metabolic dysfunction. Discusses protein lactylation in modulating the inflammatory-to-reparative phenotypic transition in AKI.
